Ahmadnagar was a sultanate in the northwestern Deccan of India, ruled by the Nizam Shahi dynasty from 1490 to 1636. Malik Ahmad, a Bahmani governor, broke away and founded the city of Ahmadnagar as his capital. It was one of the five Deccan sultanates and joined their victory over Vijayanagara in 1565.

Its later history is a long fight with the Mughals:

  • In 1595 the regent Chand Bibi held the fort against the army of Akbar. The Mughals took the city in 1600.
  • Malik Ambar, an Ethiopian born former slave, kept the state alive for two decades as its regent, fighting with fast light cavalry.
  • Shah Jahan ended it in 1636.

Shahaji, father of the Maratha king Shivaji, served as one of its last commanders. The map still shows it to 1650.
